A.explanation: Too small by about $10^{-14}$. It comes from multiplying all three quantities instead of dividing by area $6.25 \times 10^{-8} \text{ m}^2$.

B.explanation: Too small by about $10^{-9}$. It comes from dividing by length instead of multiplying by length $2.50 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$ or mishandling powers of 10.

D.explanation: Too large by about a factor of 7. It does not follow from $2.3 \times 2.50 / 6.25 = 0.92$ with the $10^{-3}$ power from $L/A$.

hints: Notice the three numbers given: resistivity $2.3 \times 10^{-8} \text{ } \Omega \text{ m}$, length $2.50 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$ and area $6.25 \times 10^{-8} \text{ m}^2$.
Recall how resistance depends on length and area: longer means larger resistance and wider area means smaller resistance, given by $R = \rho L / A$.
Set up $(2.3 \times 10^{-8} \times 2.50 \times 10^{-3}) / (6.25 \times 10^{-8})$ and simplify $2.3 \times 2.50 / 6.25$ and the powers of 10 separately.
walkthrough: Identify the given data for the gold wire: $L = 2.50 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, $A = 6.25 \times 10^{-8} \text{ m}^2$ and $\rho = 2.3 \times 10^{-8} \text{ } \Omega \text{ m}$.
State the governing relation for resistivity: $R = \rho L / A$. Resistance increases with length and resistivity and decreases with cross-sectional area.
Substitute the values with units: $R = (2.3 \times 10^{-8} \text{ } \Omega \text{ m})(2.50 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}) / (6.25 \times 10^{-8} \text{ m}^2)$.
Calculate the number part and power part separately: number part $= 2.3 \times 2.50 / 6.25 = 5.75 / 6.25 = 0.92$, power part $= 10^{-8} \times 10^{-3} / 10^{-8} = 10^{-3}$.
Combine to get $R = 0.92 \times 10^{-3} \text{ } \Omega = 9.2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ } \Omega$, with unit $\Omega$ as required. This is option C.
